summary.headline: Kirloskar Brothers Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to Rs12,767 million, but international EBITDA margin fell to 5.3% and order intake jumped 68%.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue grew 24% YoY to Rs12,767 million and EBITDA grew 16% to Rs1,432 million at an 11.2% margin, while consolidated order intake rose 68% YoY to Rs20,472 million. Standalone domestic revenue grew 23% to Rs7,991 million with PAT up 45% to Rs544 million, but standalone gross margin compressed about 400 bps, which management attributed to commodity cost inflation. The international (SPP UK, SPP USA, Dutch group) business grew 24% in revenue but EBITDA margin was only 5.3%, as UK service revenue lagged and oil and gas, a lower-margin segment, ramped up. Management guided to margin recovery in H2 and to double-digit standalone revenue growth for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: margin moderated; no YoY figure stated

segments.name: Standalone domestic
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs7,991 million (+23% YoY), EBITDA Rs937 million (+37%), PAT Rs544 million (+45%). Domestic order book Rs29,264 million as of September 2026, +29% YoY, excluding small pumps order book.

segments.name: International (SPP UK, SPP USA, Dutch group)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by SPP UK, SPP USA and Dutch group. EBITDA Rs233 million at 5.3% margin, dragged by lower services contribution. Overseas pending order book Rs17,013 million, +32%.

segments.name: Small pumps (retail)
segments.commentary: Grew 12% per press release; management said roughly 50% of that came from price and the balance from volume. Small pumps order book excluded from the Rs29,264 million domestic order book.

segments.name: Power / nuclear
segments.commentary: Power order book rose from about Rs600 million to Rs700 million sequentially per analyst. Nuclear orders for canned motor pumps and primary-side safety package were valued at roughly Rs60-70 crore combined per management.

segments.name: Oil and gas (UK/US)
segments.commentary: Oil and gas order intake picked up in UK and US (Louisiana projects, CP2, Plaquemine, Qatar NFPS, Guyana), with lower margins and higher employee costs; management said this is a drag on UK margins.

guidance_outlook: Management expects margins to improve in H2 FY27; international H2 expected to be noticeably better than H1 per Alok Kirloskar.
Double-digit standalone revenue growth in FY27 over FY26 remains the target.
UK margins: absolute levels similar to CY24 / FY25 levels expected next year, but oil and gas mix may keep margins from recovering fully until the following year.
Standalone gross margin compression attributed to commodity price rise (copper, gun metal, steel); expected to normalise over next few quarters.
Services share of SPP UK business is about 35%; target about 40% at KBI BV level over a 3-year cycle.
capex_capacity: Large consignments are pending dispatch, causing higher inventory; management expects these to go out in subsequent months, reducing inventory and lifting margins.
Working capital rose roughly Rs225 crore standalone and about Rs250 crore consolidated in H1, per analyst; management attributed it to WIP for long-lead capital goods (8-12 month lead times).

Nuclear: 32 primary coolant pumps tender for three plants (NPCIL/Tarapur); bids reportedly open 21 January 2027, first technical bid then financial bid. Casting qualification passed; a foundry was found.
demand_pricing: Standalone price increase of about 10% taken since January, per analyst; management says the company is a price leader and passes through commodity costs to a large extent.
Competitors facing supply issues (foundry closures, LPG shortage, wage code changes), which management says is enhancing market share.
Thermal, nuclear, oil and gas, fertilizer and power are driving capital goods orders; data centres in India are just starting.
UK domestic industrial demand is weak per management (electricity at Rs30/unit); growth is from oil and gas exports, data centres and fire pumps for warehousing; AMP8 not yet material.
Fire pump market worldwide about $0.5 billion, increasingly commoditised by Chinese FM/UL-certified entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Will international margins recover in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Margins expected to rise in H2, with the UK's fourth quarter (Jan-Mar) seeing more service contracts kick off; UK service business was down in the first two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How much of UK margin recovery is expected and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Alok Kirloskar said FY26 UK margins were about 7%; FY27 will recover but not to FY25 levels. Material cost up 8% in UK, and oil and gas mix lowers margins; next year similar margins to CY24 in absolute terms, with percentage recovery likely later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of small pump growth between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Rama Kirloskar said about 50% of the 12% growth came from value (price) and the balance from volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear order value and tender status?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar said canned motor pump and primary-side safety package orders together are about Rs60-70 crore. Tender for 32 primary coolant pumps issued; company says material qualification is now proven.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone gross margin compress and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed compression to commodity price rises, not legacy contracts or mix; said it will normalise over coming quarters and there is no material gap between small pumps and engineered pumps.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a 15% margin aspiration in 1-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Kirloskar declined to give a figure, saying competition for nuclear and power orders will be strong and pricing depends on operations and material costs.

risks_watch: International EBITDA margin at 5.3% with UK services lagging; margin recovery depends on services contracts kicking off in Q3/Q4 FY27.
Standalone gross margin compression of about 400 bps tied to commodity inflation; pass-through may moderate.
Rising inventory and working capital (WIP) pending dispatch; liquidation timing uncertain.
Order intake is lumpy; management said orders are recognised only once commercial terms are agreed.
Nuclear PCP tender outcome and whether margins hold under competition; the first pump at Tarapur is untested.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order intake and domestic growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on UK/international margins, which management tied to oil and gas mix, service timing and material costs. Several answers on nuclear margins and data centre timelines were deliberately non-committal.
key_quotes: Margins to go up in the second half.
I've always said that we shouldn't look at this company from quarter-to-quarter.
We are price leaders and always the first ones to increase prices, we expect this to get moderated in the next few quarters.
There was no such single large order. I mean, nothing material as it is defined.

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit standalone revenue growth for FY27 (midpoint taken as 10%), backed by a domestic order book of Rs29,264m (+29% YoY), overseas pending orders of Rs17,013m (+32%), and a ~10% price increase, with no new capacity disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided international H2 margins noticeably better than H1 (H1 consolidated EBITDA margin 11.5%, international Q2 at 5.3%), with UK service contracts kicking off in Jan-Mar and standalone gross margin (down about 400 bps on commodity costs) expected to normalise over the next few quarters, though UK FY27 margins are not expected to return to FY25 levels.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone domestic order book Rs29,264m (+29% YoY) and overseas pending orders Rs17,013m (+32%) support double-digit standalone FY27 growth guidance; small pumps grew 12% with about half from volume, and competitor supply issues are helping share gains.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure or capex plan was disclosed and no new plant, line or land was mentioned; the call discusses working capital tied to WIP, not new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only held double-digit standalone revenue growth for FY27 and did not raise it, while standalone gross margin fell about 400 bps and international EBITDA margin was 5.3%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: International EBITDA margin of 5.3% in Q2 depends on UK service contracts starting in Jan-Mar, and oil and gas mix and material costs (UK material cost up 8%) could keep margins below FY25 levels; a slip in services timing would hit H2.

rows.label: Nuclear primary coolant pump tender (32 pumps, 3 Tarapur plants)
rows.why: Bids reportedly open 21 Jan 2027 with technical then financial stages; casting qualification passed and a foundry found, but canned motor pump and safety package orders total only about Rs60-70 crore and the first Tarapur pump is untested.

rows.label: Standalone price pass-through after ~10% increase
rows.why: A ~10% price increase was taken since January and management says it passes commodity costs through to a large extent, which should help offset the ~400 bps standalone gross margin compression as costs normalise.

rows.label: Release of pending large consignments and WIP
rows.why: Working capital rose about Rs225 crore standalone and about Rs250 crore consolidated in H1 on WIP for 8-12 month lead-time capital goods; management expects pending consignments to dispatch in subsequent months, reducing inventory.
